nodes.description: Correction rather than knockdown. Dual-AAV delivery of the adenine base editor ABE8e corrected 21.4 to 28.9 per cent of alleles in the organ of Corti of a p.G321S knockin mouse, lowered auditory brainstem response thresholds by up to 49 dB SPL, and preserved hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons and nerve fibres for at least 32 weeks. nodes.description:
A second aggravating exposure, and one with a mechanism that meets this disease's own lesion rather than merely sharing its target cell. KCNQ channel activity requires PIP2, and aminoglycosides sequester PIP2. Applied intracellularly to rat outer hair cells they inhibit I(K,n) through PIP2 depletion - the same conductance the KCNQ4 variant has already reduced. So the ototoxicity that makes aminoglycosides hazardous to anyone is, in DFNA2A, a second hit on the surviving channel population.
Recorded as an inferred interaction, not a demonstrated one: the PIP2 work was done in wild-type rat outer hair cells, not in a DFNA2A model, and no study has tested aminoglycoside exposure against a KCNQ4 genotype. The convergence is on the conductance, which is what makes it worth stating.

nodes.description: A later and more contested stage. In a Kcnq4 knockout backcrossed onto the C3H/HeJ background, inner hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons die as well as outer hair cells, roughly thirty weeks later. This matters clinically because losing outer hair cells alone reduces sensitivity but does not abolish hearing, whereas losing inner hair cells and their neurons does - so this node, not the one above, is the candidate explanation for the profound late-stage deafness. Note that the finding is background-dependent in mice, which is the main reason it is recorded as a distinct node under an open hypothesis rather than as settled mechanism.

nodes.description: A pharmacological rescue strategy tested in vitro. Zinc pyrithione combined with retigabine potentiates KCNQ4 currents, and in a dominant-negative co-expression system restored current essentially to wild-type levels - probably by strongly activating the small remaining fraction of homomeric wild-type channels rather than by fixing the mutant. The critical limitation is allele-dependence: pore mutants are completely unresponsive, so the strategy cannot help the patients carrying the commonest hotspot variant. No clinical data exist.

nodes.description: Kv7.4 is a homotetramer, so a mutant subunit that still assembles but cannot conduct removes the function of every channel it joins. This is why most DFNA2A variants are dominant rather than recessive, and why the defect is far greater than the 50 per cent expected from losing one allele: co-expressing wild-type KCNQ4 with a pore mutant suppresses current to barely detectable levels. Pore-region variants and proximal C-terminal variants behave differently under pharmacological rescue, which is the first hint that this node is not a single lesion.

nodes.description:
The minority route, and the one the rest of this pathograph does not model. A small number of DFNA2 families carry variants that truncate the peptide - a frameshift before the first transmembrane domain, and stop codons removing the S5, S6 and C-terminal regions. A subunit that never reaches the tetramer poisons nothing, so on this route the surviving channel population is built from the intact allele alone and the proposed mechanism is haploinsufficiency rather than negative dominance. The reported clinical difference runs the same way: haploinsufficient alleles give later-onset high-frequency loss than the dominant-negative pore variants do.
Recorded as an open mechanism, not a settled one, and the counter-evidence is here rather than in a footnote. Heterozygous Kcnq4 knockout mice - the direct animal test of halved dose - do not lose hearing, which argues that one intact allele is tolerated and that something other than simple dosage accounts for the human truncating families. The systematic survey of every possible KCNQ4 missense substitution leaves the same question open for its large partially-rescued class, naming dominant negativity and haploinsufficiency side by side without separating them.

I(K,n) is the large standing potassium conductance active at the outer hair cell resting potential. It is the exit route for potassium that enters through the apical mechanotransduction channels, and it is what holds the cell hyperpolarised at rest. Kv7.4 carries the predominant part of it, so losing the channel removes the conductance rather than reducing it.

nodes.description: The only non-mammalian model in this entry, and it tests a different thing from the mouse lines. Where the mouse models carry a specific human-equivalent allele and are read out as progressive adult hearing loss, this is an acute knockdown read out as inner ear development: otolith morphology, hair cell number, and the startle-driven motor response. Its value is the rescue arm - the phenotype is reversed by reintroducing wild-type kcnq4 mRNA, which is the control that makes the knockdown attributable to the gene rather than to morpholino toxicity. The same paper characterizes a novel human variant, p.Trp275Cys, adjacent to the W276 hotspot.
